title: Evaluation of Hepatitis C Test and Treat Interventions Targeted at Homeless Populations (Outside London) in England During the COVID-19 Pandemic
file_title: Evaluation of hepatitis C test and treat interventions targeted at homeless populations (outside London) in England duri
description: This document describes an evaluation of hepatitis C test and treat interventions for homeless populations in England outside of London during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The interventions aimed to increase testing and treatment uptake among this high-risk group, with a focus on overcoming barriers exacerbated by the pandemic. Methodologically, the evaluation employed the Donabedian model, considering structure, processes, outputs, and outcomes, and utilized questionnaires, data fields, and structured conversations for data collection. Results indicated a 63.6% testing uptake, with 17.7% testing positive for HCV antibodies and 10.5% for current infection, particularly among drug users. Recommendations include enhancing partnerships, destigmatizing HCV, using incentives, flexible testing methods, and initiating treatment outside clinical settings. The report also discusses the challenges and successes of outreach efforts, the importance of peer support, and the need for ongoing monitoring and evaluation. Key findings show high treatment initiation rates, with variations across regions and demographic groups, and the report underscores the critical role of tailored interventions and rapid response in addressing hepatitis C among the homeless during a public health crisis.

title: Evaluation of the 'Be Clear on Cancer' lung cancer awareness campaign: Regional pilot, East and West Midlands, 10 October to 13 November 2011
file_title: Evaluation of the 'Be Clear on Cancer' lung cancer awareness campaign: regional pilot, East and West Midlands, 10 Octobe
description: This document summarizes the evaluation of the Be Clear on Cancer lung cancer awareness campaign in the East and West Midlands, which aimed to promote early diagnosis and treatment of lung cancer, particularly targeting individuals over 50 from lower socio-economic groups. The campaign was a collaborative effort by Public Health England, the Department of Health, NHS England, and Cancer Research UK. The evaluation employed surveys, analysis of campaign materials, and tracking of patient pathways to measure its impact. Results showed an increase in awareness and earlier diagnosis, with a rise in GP attendances and urgent referrals for suspected lung cancer, as well as an increase in lung cancer diagnoses and surgical resection rates. However, there was no significant change in attitudes towards cancer or in the use of diagnostic tests. The campaign effectively reached its audience without overburdening NHS services, despite some challenges. Data from various NHS trusts contributed to the evaluation, but specific results and conclusions from this aspect of the evaluation are not provided in the text.

title: Phase 1: Evaluation of the NHS Weight Loss Plan App
file_title: Better Health campaign phase 1: evaluation of the NHS weight loss plan app
description: This document describes an evaluation of the NHS 12-week weight loss plan, a component of the Better Health campaign, aimed at promoting healthier diets and physical activity, particularly for weight management in response to COVID-19 risks. The evaluation, conducted by the University of Leeds and The James Hutton Institute, analyzed app usage data from July 2020 to February 2021. Results indicated that users, especially those who completed the program, experienced significant weight loss, with variations across gender, age, and BMI categories. The majority of users were female, over 40, and overweight or obese. Despite over 800,000 downloads, the completion rate was low, suggesting a need for strategies to improve user retention. Recommendations include tailoring the app to diverse ethnic groups and exploring alternatives to calorie counting. The evaluation also highlighted the potential for the app to positively impact population health, despite high dropout rates and the necessity for further research to understand user engagement and address health inequalities.
